statement: A line 'First Last' is given. Print 'Last, First'. Use indexOf(" ") and substring.

title: While: count from 1 to 5
statement: The code below should print the numbers 1 to 5, one per line. Fill in the blanks.

title: Tracing a while loop
solution: Correct answer: C) -2

title: Countdown
statement: A number N is given. Print every number from N down to 1, one per line, then print 'Go!'. Use a while loop.

title: Infinite loop
statement: This program should compute the sum 1 + 2 + ... + N, but it runs forever. Find the bug and fix it.

title: While: running total
statement: The code below should print the sum 5+4+3+2+1.

title: Sum of digits
statement:
A positive integer N is given. Print the sum of its digits. (e.g. 1234 -> 10)
Hint: n % 10 is the last digit, n / 10 removes it.

title: Reverse a number (bug)
statement: This program should reverse the number N (1234 -> 4321, 1200 -> 21) but it is wrong. Fix it.

title: Collatz steps
statement:
A number n > 0 is given. Until n = 1: if n is even do n/2, otherwise 3n+1. Print how many steps are needed. (6 -> 8 steps; 1 -> 0 steps)
Use long for n and the intermediate values.

title: GCD (Euclid)
statement: Two positive integers a and b are given on one line. Find and print their greatest common divisor using Euclid's algorithm (inside a while loop).

title: Palindromic number
statement: A positive integer N is given. Without using Strings, print YES if the number equals its reverse, otherwise NO.

title: Trailing zeros of a factorial
statement:
Print how many zeros are at the end of N!. 1 <= N <= 1,000,000,000 (you cannot compute N!, think!).
Hint: each zero comes from a 2x5 pair; 5s are rarer.

title: Reverse a word
statement: A single word is given. Print its letters in reverse order. (java -> avaj)

title: Vowel counter
statement: The program should count the vowels (a e i o u) in the word but it throws an error. Fix it.

title: Palindromic word
statement: A single word is given. Print YES if the word equals its reverse, otherwise NO.

title: Caesar cipher
statement: A shift k and then a lowercase word are given. Shift every letter k places forward in the alphabet (after z comes a) and print it. (3 abc -> def)

title: Count occurrences
statement:
A text is given on the first line and a pattern on the second. Print how many times the pattern appears in the text, counting overlaps. (in 'aaaa', 'aa' -> 3)
Hint: use indexOf(pattern, start).

title: Run-length encoding
statement: A word of lowercase letters is given. Compress consecutive equal letters as letter+count. (aaabcc -> a3b1c2)

title: Counter class
statement:
Write a Counter class:
• Counter()  — the counter starts at 0
• void increment()  — adds 1
• void reset()  — sets it back to 0
• int getCount()  — returns the current value

title: Rectangle class
statement:
Write a Rectangle class:
• Rectangle(int width, int height)
• int getArea()
• int getPerimeter()
• boolean isSquare()

title: BankAccount class
statement:
Write a BankAccount class:
• BankAccount(double initial)
• void deposit(double amount)  — adds it if amount > 0
• boolean withdraw(double amount)  — if amount > 0 and does not exceed the balance, withdraws it and returns true; otherwise does nothing and returns false
• double getBalance()

title: GradeBook class
statement:
Write a GradeBook class:
• GradeBook()
• void addGrade(int g)
• int getCount()
• double getAverage()  — 0.0 if there are no grades
• int getHighest()  — 0 if there are no grades

title: Point class
statement:
Write a Point class:
• Point(int x, int y)
• int getX(), int getY()
• double distanceTo(Point other)  — Euclidean distance
• String toString()  — in the form "(x, y)", e.g. (3, -4)

title: static helper methods
statement:
Write a MathUtils class. All methods must be static:
• static boolean isPrime(int n)  — n < 2 is not prime
• static int factorial(int n)  — n >= 0
• static int gcd(int a, int b)

title: Fraction class
statement:
Write a Fraction class:
• Fraction(int num, int den)  — reduces the fraction; if the denominator is negative, moves the sign to the numerator (den != 0)
• Fraction add(Fraction other)  — returns a new Fraction
• String toString()  — "a/b"; just "a" if the denominator is 1

title: Library and Book (ArrayList)
statement:
Write two classes:
Book: Book(String title, String author), String getTitle(), String getAuthor()
Library: Library(), void addBook(Book b), int countByAuthor(String author), ArrayList<String> titlesBy(String author)  — titles in the order added
Hint: don't forget import java.util.*;

title: Inheritance: Animal, Dog, Cat
statement:
Write three classes:
Animal: Animal(String name), String getName(), String sound() returns "...", String describe() returns "<name> says <sound()>"
Dog extends Animal: sound() returns "Woof"
Cat extends Animal: sound() returns "Meow"
describe() must be written only in Animal; polymorphism must work.

title: Card and Comparable
statement:
Write a Card class that implements Comparable<Card>:
• Card(int rank, String suit)  — rank 1..13
• int getRank(), String getSuit()
• String toString()  — rank label + suit; labels: 1->A, 11->J, 12->Q, 13->K, others are the number. e.g. "AS", "10H", "KD"
• int compareTo(Card o)  — orders by rank first, then by suit (using compareTo)
Collections.sort(list) must work.
